column4: Visit note | 2025-03-12 11:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tushar Bhattacharya, 31, male. Mr. Bhattacharya reports a burning sensation behind his breastbone after meals that becomes worse when lying down, along with a sour taste in his mouth. He mentions these symptoms feel worse after weeks of eating fried snacks at tea stalls in Dhanmondi. He works as a homemaker, lives with his family, and denies any prior history of stomach problems. On examination: BMI 31.1, BP 123/84 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 63 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness without guarding. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-03-12 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Mitu Shikder, 80, female. Mrs. Shikder describes losing weight without trying, cuts that take a long time to heal, and an unquenchable thirst. She notes these changes started after a relative in Badda was diagnosed and advised testing. She works as a farmer and lives with her children. On examination: fasting glucose 11.4 mmol/L, BP 132/85 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 58 kg. Examination is otherwise unremarkable with clear chest and normal heart sounds. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check her feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-03-16 10:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Selim Chowdhury, 19, male. Mr. Chowdhury states he has troublesome pimples and blackheads on his face alongside spots on his back. He explains the condition became worse since working in a hot kitchen in Faridpur. He is a hotel receptionist and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: about 35 inflamed spots on the face, BP 134/78 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 69 kg. Skin is oily with scattered papules and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-03-16 03:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Hasina Molla, 19, female. Miss Molla presents complaining of a throbbing headache on one side of her head accompanied by sensitivity to bright light. She reports about 8 headache days a month, which she notices are triggered by skipping meals while travelling in Rampura. She is a university student and lives in a hostel. On examination: BP 127/76 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 49 kg. Neurological examination shows no focal deficits, normal cranial nerves, and normal fundoscopy. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-03-24 09:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Shafiq Pramanik, 20, male. Mr. Pramanik complains of spots on his back along with pimples and blackheads on his face. He mentions the skin flare-up became worse since working in a hot kitchen in Jashore. He works as a journalist and has Essential hypertension. On examination: about 11 inflamed spots on the face, BP 147/86 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 46 kg. Skin shows moderate acne lesions without scarring. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and not to squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.
